2. Challenging judgment and award dated 06.06.2018 passed by Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chittapur, (for short, 'Tribunal') in MVC no.05/2017, this appeal is filed.
3.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chittapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Sri Sanjeev Patil, learned counsel submitted, appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted, on 29.12.2011, while claimant working as Police Constable was on patrolling duty, rider of Bajaj Discover motorcycle bearing Chassis no.MD2DHZZUCE77272 and Engine no.DHGBUE54595, rode it in rash and negligent manner, lost control, dashed against claimant and caused accident.
Despite taking treatment at Chittapur Government Hospital and Global Hospital, Hyderabad, he did not recover fully and sustained NC: 2025:KHC-K:3807 HC-KAR permanent physical disability.
Therefore, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, against owner and insurer of motorcycle.

4. On contest, wherein, claim petition was opposed denying rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider as well as denying age, occupation, income and disability sustained by claimant, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant examined himself as PW.1 and Exs.P1 to P12 were marked.
Respondents did not lead evidence.

5. On consideration, tribunal held accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider and claimant was entitled for compensation from insurer as follows:

sentences.text: Sl. No

. Heads of Compensation Amount 1 Pain and suffering Rs. 25,000/- 2 Medical expenses Rs.1,53,000/- 3 Diet and attendant charges Rs. 20,000/- 4 Loss of future earnings Nil 5 Loss of salary during treatment Rs. 2,360/-
period Total Rs.2,00,360/-

Rounded off to Rs.2,00,000/-
 6.

Dissatisfied with quantum of compensation,
claimant is in appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:3807 HC-KAR 7.
Sole ground urged for enhancement was though claimant was a Government employee, he had sustained permanent physical disability, tribunal denied compensation towards future loss of income.
It erred in not awarding any compensation towards loss of amenities.

It was submitted,
since disability would affect claimant even while he was not on employment, compensation ought to be substantial under said head.
8. On other hand, Sri Rahul R.Asture, learned counsel for respondent-insurer opposed appeal.

It was submitted, insurer had satisfied award and as there was no loss of earning capacity,
compensation awarded was just and proper and there was no scope for enhancement.
9.
Heard learned counsel.
Perused impugned judgment and award.

10. From above and since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation while insurer has accepted award, point that would arise for consideration is:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:3807 HC-KAR "Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
11.
Since insurer has accepted award, occurrence of accident, claimant sustaining permanent physical disability and being entitled for compensation are not in dispute.
Claimant was 28 years old, working as Police Constable.
As per Ex.P7- disability report, claimant sustained 40% disability on account of mal-union of fracture of right tibia and fibula with restriction of movement and wastage of muscles.
Taking same into account and fact that claimant has not been awarded any compensation towards loss of future income, it would be appropriate to award Rs.75,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Thus, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

Consequently,
